title: Add region-binding enforcer and KMS usage provenance logger
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Customers with strict data residency needs asked for stronger enforcement and traceability when operator actions route to cross-region KMS providers. This PR implements a lightweight region-binding enforcer middleware and a KMS usage provenance logger that attaches provider provenance into audit envelopes and de-duplicates noisy retry-era audit records. Motivation: reduce incident risk from accidental cross-region key usage, provide cryptographically linkable provenance in audit logs for compliance reviews, and make RBAC v2 role templates available for regional operator constraints. What changed: 1) Add region-binding-enforcer service that validates tenant/route allowed geozones and either rejects requests or issues an annotated consent hint for allowed fallbacks. 2) Add kms_provenance_logger that annotates audit records with KMS provider id, key origin region, invocation-path hash, and provenance-level (e.g., primary|fallback). 3) Audit dedupe: implement operation-id-based dedupe in audit ingestion to collapse repeated entries from transparent retries within a 30s window. 4) RBAC v2: introduce region_operator role template and automated generation script for service-level bindings. 5) Tests, docs, and a console docs page describing the feature flags and rollout strategy. Rollout plan: dark-launch under feature flag region_binding_v1 in staging for 48h; enable to 5% of traffic in canary for two days; then full rollout. Backout plan: toggle feature flag off; revert single migration that adds the dedupe index. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for enforcer and logger - [x] Integration tests against mock KMS providers - [x] OPA policy and conftest validations - [x] Docs and console entry - [x] Devops runbook for rollback and audit migration Notes: this is not a hard KMS migration; the service reads the KMS provider metadata the gateway already forwards. See linked tasks for gateway header contract. Related: ENG-4321, SEC-118.

review_comments: Diego Moreno: Nice separation between enforcer and gateway-level checks. Question: should the enforcer ever auto-fallback to a consent-derived region? Suggest making that explicit via a new response header rather than implicit.
Aisha Patel: Reply: Agreed. Current implementation emits X-Region-Consent-Hint and never performs silent fallback. Added tests to assert header presence.
Lena Fischer: Security review: please ensure the provenance token cannot be spoofed by downstreams. Recommend HMAC with service signing key.
Aisha Patel: Reply: Implemented HMAC signing of the provenance blob using the internal audit signing key. See kms_provenance_logger.go lines adding SignProvenance().
Samir Gupta: Ops: audit dedupe uses an in-memory cache and a DB index. Can we fall back to DB-only mode for multi-replica deployments?
Aisha Patel: Reply: Yes. Dedupe implementation has a pluggable backend. Default tries memcache then DB dedupe index. Documented in the runbook.
